current.text: He is a projected starter next to Scoot Henderson, Damian Lillard, Deni Avdija and Donovan Clingan.
Portland has a first-time head coach who may mix up the lineup.
His minutes look safe. The team likely needs him for about 34 minutes a night, and the rotation is thin at forward after the eighth man.
Portland has several on-ball guards in Lillard, Ja Morant, Henderson and Jrue Holiday.
His usage is expected to shrink further with Henderson, Lillard and Morant around.
Experts say he should not be drafted in 12-team leagues, and a rank near 101 is too high for him.
Portland plays 10 games in the fantasy playoff weeks for a season ending March 28, which the expert calls weak. Three of the playoff games are back-to-backs.

durable.text: He is an elite defender and the only real point-of-attack defender on Portland's roster.
His fantasy value rests mostly on steals and threes. He gives little in the other categories.
His shooting runs in hot and cold stretches. He shot poorly for most of last season and only improved in the last six weeks.
He has weak ball handling and is seen as a poor finisher.
He has missed very few games over the last two seasons.

note: Camara sits on the edge of our 144-player pool (Yahoo rank 109, ESPN rank 131) and costs almost nothing: 3 USD Yahoo value, 0 USD ESPN, 4 USD in our league last season. The newest expert call is to skip him in 12-team drafts, because Portland's guards take most of the usage and he offers mainly steals and about 2 threes a game, with below-average FG%, FT% and assists. His starting job and roughly 30 to 34 minutes look safe, so leave him for a last-dollar pick or for waivers. Early in the season, check whether his shooting holds and his steals climb back toward 1.5, and keep in mind Portland's weak 10-game playoff schedule.
